## Verdict

**Acme Desk** costs least for a team of 35, at **$280 per month**. Its $8 per-seat rate is the lowest on the list, and its 10-seat minimum sits well below the team size, so all 35 seats bill at list with nothing wasted. Fennel HQ is $420 and Kelp is $850 — Kelp's 50-seat minimum forces payment for 15 seats the team will not use.

## Vendor pricing

| Vendor | Price per seat | Minimum seats |
|---|---|---|
| Acme Desk | $8 | 10 |
| Fennel HQ | $12 | 25 |
| Kelp | $17 | 50 |

## Cost at this size

Seats paid for = the greater of 35 (team size) or the vendor minimum.

- **Acme Desk:** minimum 10 < 35, so 35 seats paid. 35 × $8 = **$280 per month**. Effective rate $8.00 per person.
- **Fennel HQ:** minimum 25 < 35, so 35 seats paid. 35 × $12 = **$420 per month**. Effective rate $12.00 per person.
- **Kelp:** minimum 50 > 35, so 50 seats paid. 50 × $17 = **$850 per month**. Effective rate $24.29 per person ($850 ÷ 35), against a listed $17.

Acme Desk is $140 per month cheaper than Fennel HQ and $570 per month cheaper than Kelp. Over twelve months that is $1,680 and $6,840 respectively.

## Risks

Only Kelp is penalised by its minimum at this size, and that penalty disappears at 50 seats — but even then Kelp bills $17 per seat against Acme Desk's $8, so Acme Desk stays cheapest at every headcount above 10. Below 10 people, Acme Desk bills a $80 floor; Fennel HQ and Kelp bill $300 and $850 respectively, so the ranking does not change on the way down either.

This comparison covers list price only. The price list carries no information on features, support tiers, usage limits, security posture, or integrations, so a cheaper seat may buy a smaller product — that gap is unmeasured here.

All figures assume monthly billing at list, as stated. Annual commitments, volume discounts, onboarding fees, and overage charges are not in the source and could change the totals. Confirm whether seat minimums are enforced at signup or only at renewal, since that determines the cost of shrinking.
